product_context: Paraform (Agentic Hiring Platform) — not a Dune Security feature. Written for a design take-home exercise; source material is the exercise prompt, not an internal spec.
key_fields: visibility toggle (Visible to Para AI / Private to recruiter)
integrations: Para AI matching layer (platform-wide, surfaces matches beyond the recruiter's own submissions)
open_questions_flagged: What is the default approval-required timeout window before escalation?
Does the candidate ever see any part of this system, or is it recruiter/Para-AI only?
How are cross-opportunity conflicts (e.g., same-company double submission) detected — real-time rule check or periodic reconciliation?
What happens to Para AI's confidence in a candidate profile when a majority of sources are marked private?
Does Paraform perform any identity resolution across independently-owned recruiter profiles for the same real person, to catch duplicate submissions to the same role from different recruiters?
Can Para AI surface a match to an opportunity the recruiter hasn't chosen, and does entering it always require recruiter confirmation the same way a recruiter-initiated submission does?
confidence_notes: Single source (the take-home prompt itself) with no existing Figma or internal spec to cross-reference. Scope, actors, and edge cases were reasonably inferable from the prompt and the linked Passive Placements concept, but several judgment calls (default visibility rules, approval timeout window, conflict-detection mechanism) are design decisions made to produce a complete PRD rather than facts confirmed by the source. Updated 2026-07-11 with further product research indicating candidate profiles are owned per recruiter (not shared platform-wide) and that Para AI's matching reach can extend beyond opportunities the recruiter has directly pursued — this is a working hypothesis pending confirmation, not a PM-confirmed fact, and is tracked as open questions.
